html:
A set of laws that kept people who were not of European origin from settling in Australia, from Federation in 1901 until 1973.

Hostility to Chinese diggers in the gold rushes and to Pacific Island workers brought in by blackbirding had already led the colonies to pass anti-Chinese laws. When the colonies joined in the Federation of Australia, one of the first acts of the new parliament was the Immigration Restriction Act of 1901. It used a dictation test: an official could make a migrant write out 50 words in any European language, chosen to make sure they failed. Most Pacific Islanders were deported.

The policy had wide support in all parties for decades. After the Second World War, the drive for postwar migration brought in southern and eastern Europeans, and the rules for Asians were slowly eased from the late 1940s. The government of Gough Whitlam ended race as a factor in 1973.

Within a few years Australia took in thousands of Vietnamese refugees, and today a large share of its people have Asian roots.
sum: A set of laws that kept people who were not of European origin from settling in Australia, from Federation in 1901 until 1973.
